No worries. I'll give some feedback later today or tomorrow.

Formatting / presentation
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly as described in the points below.

Goal
* Using the term "AI" seems unnecessary, as the task is independent of whether the solver is human or AI.

* Several aspects of the task are currently unclear. For example:

  • [[N]] is used before it's explicitly defined.

  • It's unclear whether every server must be visited.

• Please rewrite and format this section as follows (excluding the "-----" dividers):

-----
You are tasked with routing a critical data packet through a temporally unstable network.

<<Network>>

The network consists of [[N]] servers, numbered from {{0}} to [[N]] - {{1}}, and [[M]] directed temporal links. Each link connects two servers.

<<Packet>>

The packet starts at server {{0}} at time {{0}} with an initial stability energy of [[E_max]]. Traversing a link consumes stability energy and takes a fixed amount of time.

If the packet's stability energy drops below {{0}}, it is destroyed.

<<Movement and Stability Energy>>

The packet does not need to visit every server. It may pause and wait at any server for any amount of time without consuming stability energy.

Because the network is collapsing, each link is active only during specific, possibly fragmented time windows. The packet can traverse a link only if:

• it has sufficient stability energy to complete the traversal, and

• the <<entire>> traversal fits within a single active window of that link. The entire traversal runs from its departure time [[t]] through its arrival time [[t]] + [[dt]], where [[dt]] is the time required to traverse the link.

The packet can also restore its stability energy repeatedly at certain servers. Each server has a <<restoration efficiency>>, defined as the time required to restore {{1}} unit of stability energy. Restoration is unavailable at servers where the efficiency is {{-1}}.

Stability energy is restored in whole units and can never exceed [[E_max]].

<<Objective>>

Your objective is to determine the earliest possible time at which the packet can reach server [[N]] - {{1}} without being destroyed. If the destination cannot be reached, output {{UNREACHABLE}}.
-----

Input

* Some descriptions currently placed in the Input section belong to the Goal section. Some of the points below specify how such descriptions should be revised.

* Please format all variable names, e.g. [[N]] instead of N.

* Please format "Line 1", "Line 2" and "Next [[M]] lines" in <<bold>>.

* Please replace all instances of "node(s)" with "server(s)".

* Line 1 & Next M lines: Please list every variable on its own line for easier reading. For example,

<<Line 1>>: 3 space-separated integers:
[[N]]: number of servers
[[M]]: (etc.)

(continued)

* Line 2: Please rewrite as follows:

<<Line 2>>: [[N]] space-separated integers [[R]], where the values are given in order from server {{0}} to server [[N]] - 1 and represent their respective restoration efficiencies.

* Next M lines: Please change "starting with 5 integers" to "consisting of space-separated integers, starting with:".

* Consider using "start_t" and "end_t" (instead of "start_i" and "end_i") as these names make the meaning of the variables clearer. If this is adopted, please update the Constraints section accordingly.

* Please remove the note at the end of the section, as it's incorporated into the revised Goal section.

Output
* Please change "N-1" to "[[N]] - {{1}}".

* Please format "UNREACHABLE" as a {{constant}}.

Constraints
* Please change "R_i" to "R"

* Please add:

0 ≤ [[u]], [[v]] < [[N]]
Active windows for a given link never overlap.
For every link, [[u]] ≠ [[v]].
For any two links, [[u]] and [[v]] cannot both be the same.

* Please reorder the constraints so that they appear in the same order as the variables in the input.

* Please format all [[variables]].

* Please format -1 as a {{constant}}.

* The upper bounds of some variables are overstated compared with the maximum values used in the cases. Unless cases that exercise the full ranges in a reasonably balanced manner are introduced, please revise them as follows:

  • N, M, E_max, R: 10

  • dt, end_i: 100  

Difficulty
* It may be possible to reclassify the puzzle as Medium instead of Hard, but the final classification should be determined based on the final test case set and the resulting algorithmic difficulty.

Cases
* Please use a wider range of input values. For example, currently:

  • W is always 1.

  • start_i is 0 for most links.

  • end_i is 100 for most links.

  • N = 3 and M = 2 for over half of the cases.

  • u < v in all cases.

* What scenarios are covered by the current cases? Consider naming the cases according to the scenarios they're intended to test.

* Please ensure that the cases cover different scenarios (a test/validator pair may, of course, cover multiple scenarios at the same time):

  • A traversal starts exactly at the window start.

  • A traversal finishes exactly at the window end.

  • Waiting is required before a future window can be used.

  • Multiple feasible windows, including windows given in unsorted order.

  • Some links form cycles.

  • UNREACHABLE because there's no path from the source to the destination.

  • UNREACHABLE because every active window is too short, i.e. dt > end_i - start_i.

  • UNREACHABLE because all feasible paths miss their active windows in the final part of the paths.

  • Multiple branches from source to destination with different time costs, energy costs, active windows and restoration efficiencies.

  • A route requires energy restoration before a link can be traversed.

  • An intermediate server is reached with zero remaining energy.

(continued)

  • The destination is reached with zero remaining energy.

  • Two consecutive active windows for the same link, where end_i1 = start_i2 and dt = end_i2 - start_i1.

  • Insufficient energy causes a missed window: the packet must restore energy before traversing a link, but the time spent restoring enough energy causes the required active window to be missed.

  • The packet initially lacks sufficient energy for a link, restores the required amount, and then successfully traverses the link within the same active window when the packet initially arrives.

  • (There may still be more scenario that I might be missing…)

* Please order the cases by increasing complexity. At the beginning of the test set, introduce only one or two rules at a time so that the early cases establish the basic mechanics of the problem before progressively combining more rules and edge cases.

Thanks.
